title: Interview with Ida Bowers and Wayne Pierce
description: Oral history interview with Stan State professors Dr. Ida Bowers and Dr. Wayne Pierce - discussing their development of the Bio-Ag and Trans-California projects on the Stan State campus since the 1980s.
subject: Stan State history

bio: Dr. Ida Bowers, earned her PhD in Indonesia and started in the Department of Geography in 1972. Over her 37-year tenure on campus, she brought her students on trips as far away as Bali and other parts of Indonesia while on campus she tended to bio-agricultural project, the Trans-California Pathway, and teaching projects including sustainable farming plots and a butterfly garden. At the time of the interview, Dr. Bowers and Pierce had been teaching at the University for over thirty years each and both were retired, though one or both were teaching a class or two as part of the California State University Faculty Early Retirement Program (FERP). Dr. Wayne Pierce earned his PhD in Plant Physiology from Washington State University and began his academic career in the Department of Biology at Stan State in 1971. He served the campus community for 35 years as a professor and during those years he took on many additional roles including department chair for nine years and Faculty Athletic Representative to the NCAA for 25 years. Dr. Pierce had a vision of a Trans-California Pathway on campus that was partially completed before he passed away in 2008.

title: Interview with Donna Pierce
description: Oral history interview with educator and Trans-California Pathway founder, Donna Pierce - discussing her early life, her move with her husband to Turlock, life since 1971 at Stan State, and her leadership in the culmination of the Trans-California Pathway on campus.
subject: Stan State history

bio: Dr. Donna Martine Pierce grew up in Atascadero, California. She studied history at the University of California, Santa Barbara and then transferred and finished her degree at Washington State University. She married her childhood friend, Wayne Pierce, in 1964. She spent several years in Washington state with Wayne while he was working on his PhD in plant physiology. Donna and Wayne settled in Turlock, California in Fall 1971, as Wayne took up an assistant professor position in the biology department at Stan State. Donna spent decades working as a teacher for the California Youth Authority in Stockton, California. She spent many years supporting Stan State cultural and athletic programs. She is well known for her 25-year tenure running the shot clock at Stan State basketball games. She also briefly played for the university orchestra and coached the softball team when it started up in 1978. In 2002, Donna retired from her work with the Youth Authority.  In 2007 she was inducted into the Warrior Athletics Hall of Fame.  After Wayne passed away in 2008, Donna facilitated the development of the Trans-California Pathway (named The Wayne and Donna Pierce Trans-California Pathway in 2023). In 2024, Stan State awarded her with an honorary doctorate.
